notes.content: DIVERSITY REQUIREMENT FOR CAL STATE LA GRADUATION

The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement , not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University. For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements. Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

notes.content: The Bachelor of Science Degree in Natural Science provides broad training across several science disciplines and is offered as four options: Biology, Chemistry, Geoscience and Physics. The Natural Science degree is of value to those seeking careers where a broad science background is useful, including careers in education, business, government, law, medicine, nonprofit organizations, and other fields. In addition to providing broad science training, the degree also fulfils the content knowledge for students seeking a Single-Subject Teaching Credential, and is sufficient to waive the CSET (subject matter exam). High school preparation is recommended in algebra (two years), chemistry, geometry, physics, and trigonometry. Degree Requirements The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Natural Science is 120 units, of which 77-83 units are in the major. Students study multiple natural science disciplines, and choose one option among biology, chemistry, geoscience, and physics & astronomy. In each option students must earn a grade of C or higher in all courses that satisfy the following university, general education or major requirements.
